records.title: Ādāmōḍi Gaḷadē
records.meaning: Asks if there is anyone as forgiving and gracious as Sri Rama, who tolerates every fault of his devotees.
records.notes: Popular Charukesi kriti, often used to showcase the raga's characteristic swaras.

records.title: Anupama Guṇāmbudhi
records.pallavi: Anupama guṇāmbudhi śrī rāmā nīvē gati
records.meaning: Addresses Rama as the boundless ocean of matchless virtues, and the singer's sole refuge.
records.notes: Well-known Atana kriti, frequently taught to intermediate students.

records.title: Bāla Kanaka Maya Cēla
records.pallavi: Bāla kanaka maya cēla dharuni rāma
records.meaning: Describes the young Rama's golden robes and radiant form.
records.notes: Less frequently performed Atana kriti compared to Anupama Gunambudhi.

records.title: Baṇṭu Rīti Kolu
records.pallavi: Baṇṭu rīti kolu swāmi nīvē manasuku telisi
records.meaning: The singer offers himself as Rama's loyal servant, asking to be accepted into faithful service.
records.notes: Extremely popular concert item; one of the best-known Hamsanadam kritis.

records.title: Bhajana Sēyavē
records.meaning: Instructs the mind to simply get on with worship.

records.title: Bhāvanuta Nā Manasu
records.pallavi: Bhāvanuta nā manasu nī vasamā rāma
records.meaning: Asks whether the singer's mind, praised for its devotion, is truly under Rama's control.

records.title: Bhōgīndra Śāyinaṃ
records.meaning: Calls on the mind to worship Vishnu, who reclines upon the serpent couch.
records.notes: One of Tyagaraja's few Sanskrit compositions, set in the rare raga Kuntalavarali.

records.title: Bhuvini Dāsuḍane
records.meaning: Declares oneself a true servant of Rama in this world, questioning the sincerity of that claim.
records.notes: Composed in the ghana raga Sri; less commonly performed.

records.title: Brōva Bhāramā
records.meaning: Asks Rama whether protecting the singer is really too great a burden for him.

records.title: Cakkani Rāja Mārgamu
records.meaning: Compares surrender to Rama's grace to a clear royal road, contrasted with the crooked bylanes of other paths.
records.notes: Concert staple; often taught early for its clear structure.

records.title: Cēdē Buddi Mānurā
records.meaning: Admonishes the mind to abandon its base, harmful thoughts.

records.title: Cēsinadella Maracitivō
records.meaning: Asks Rama if he has forgotten all the good deeds the singer has done for him.

records.title: Dācukōvalenā
records.meaning: Asks why one should have to hide one's devotion in the presence of those who lack compassion.
records.notes: Major Todi concert piece, technically demanding.

records.title: Dārini Telusukoṇṭi
records.meaning: Says he has found the way, addressing the Goddess Tripurasundari of Tiruvottiyur.
records.notes: From the Tiruvoṭṭiyūr set on Devi — unusual for a composer whose work is almost entirely on Rama.

records.title: Dāśarathī Nī Ṛṇamu
records.meaning: The singer laments being unable to repay the debt of gratitude owed to Dasarathi (Rama).

records.title: Dinamaṇi Vaṃśa
records.meaning: Praises Rama as the moon risen from the nectarous ocean that is the Solar dynasty.

records.title: Dorakunā Ituvaṇṭi Sēva
records.meaning: Wonders whether such an opportunity to serve Rama will ever come again.

records.title: Duḍukugala Nannē
records.pallavi: Duḍukugala nannē dora koḍuku brōcurā entō
records.meaning: Tyagaraja calls himself a wretch full of misdeeds and asks which prince's son would trouble to save him — a catalogue of self-accusation.
records.notes: The charanams are an unsparing list of the composer's own failings. Gaula's vakra descent makes this the hardest of the five to keep in tune.

records.title: Ēlā Nī Daya Rādu
records.pallavi: Ēlā nī daya rādu rāmā nāpai
records.meaning: Asks Rama why his compassion has still not descended upon the singer.
records.notes: Aṭāṇā (also spelt Aṭana) is a rakti rāga where the gāndhāra is heavily oscillated — the scale on paper tells you very little about it.

records.title: Ēmi Jēsitēnēmi
records.meaning: Declares that whatever one does is fruitless without purity of mind.

records.title: Endarō Mahānubhāvulu
records.meaning: Salutes the countless great souls who have realised the divine — the composer bowing to everyone who came before him.
records.notes: Always sung last of the five, and the piece that closes the massed Ārādhana rendition at Tiruvaiyāru. Śrī rāga's narrow contours make the swara passages deceptively hard.

records.title: Endu Dāginādō
records.meaning: Wonders where Rama is hiding, unseen by his devotee.

records.title: Endukū Peddala
records.meaning: Questions why the young do not heed the counsel of their elders.

records.title: Enta Muddō
records.pallavi: Enta muddō enta sogasō śrī rāma bāla
records.meaning: Describes how utterly charming and beautiful the child Rama appears.
records.notes: Popular vatsalya-bhava (parental-love) kriti depicting baby Rama.

records.title: Ēṭāvunarā
records.meaning: Asks what manner of person withholds compassion, questioning Rama's delay in showing grace.

records.title: Ēṭi Janma Midi
records.pallavi: Ēṭi janma midi rāma bhakti lēka
records.meaning: Laments what kind of birth this is, lived without devotion to Rama.
records.notes: Set in Varali, one of the ghana ragas; demanding, ancient raga.

records.title: Ēṭula Brōtuvō
records.meaning: Wonders in what way Rama will ultimately choose to protect the singer.

records.title: Ēvari Māṭa Vinnavēmirā
records.meaning: Asks the mind whose advice it has been listening to, having strayed from devotion.

records.title: Giripai Nelakonna
records.meaning: Describes Lord Venkatesa, who has made his abode atop the hill.
records.notes: Popular Venkatesa kriti associated with Tirumala.

records.title: Grahabalamēmi
records.meaning: Declares that planetary influence means nothing when Rama himself is one's strength.

records.title: Heccarikagā Rārā
records.meaning: Calls Rama to come forth watchfully, alert to the devotee's plea.

records.title: Inta Saukhyamanine
records.meaning: Exclaims that no one else can be told of such happiness found in devotion to Rama.

records.title: Intakannānandamēmi
records.meaning: Asks what greater joy exists than chanting the name of Rama.

records.title: Jagadānandakāraka
records.meaning: Hails Rama as the source of the world's joy and the lord of Janaki's life — the only Pancharatna entirely in Sanskrit.
records.notes: Ten charanams, each a garland of Rama's names in Sanskrit. The one Pancharatna with no Telugu in it. Learn the pallavi and one charanam properly before attempting the whole.

records.title: Jñānamosaga Rādā
records.meaning: Pleads with Rama to grant the wisdom needed for liberation.

records.title: Kaddanuvāriki
records.meaning: Speaks of being unable to refuse those who claim to belong to oneself.

records.title: Kalyāṇamu Vaibhōgamē
records.meaning: Celebrates the splendour of Rama and Sita's wedding — sung at the marriage sequence of temple festivals.
records.notes: A ritual song for the kalyāṇōtsavam; the tala is written as khaṇḍa cāpu but many groups sing it in a relaxed Adi.

records.title: Kanakana Rucirā
records.meaning: The more he looks at the golden-robed Rama, the sweeter the sight becomes — a kriti built entirely on the pleasure of darshan.
records.notes: Varāḷi is traditionally not taught guru-to-student directly; learners pick it up by listening. Take the vakra ārōhaṇa slowly.

records.title: Karuṇājaladhi
records.meaning: Calls Rama the ocean of compassion, pleading to be governed and protected by him.

records.title: Koluvaiyunnāḍē
records.meaning: Announces that Lord Rama is present, holding court, ready to receive his devotees.

records.title: Koluvamaregadā
records.meaning: Asks Rama why he no longer holds court to receive his devotees, having hidden himself away.
records.notes: Landmark Todi masterpiece, a concert staple demanding advanced technique.

records.title: Kṣīṇamai Tiruganu
records.meaning: The singer, worn down and weakened, asks whom else he can implore for help.

records.title: Mari Mari Ninnē
records.meaning: Again and again he has pleaded — and asks how many more times he must.

records.title: Marugēlarā
records.meaning: Why the concealment, Raghava? — asks why Rama hides himself from one who has no other refuge.
records.notes: Jayantasēna is used for almost nothing else, so the rāga and the kriti are learnt together.

records.title: Mēru Samāna
records.meaning: Praises Rama as steady as Mount Meru.
records.notes: One of the few concert kritis in Māyāmāḷavagauḷa, the rāga every student begins with in varisai practice.

records.title: Mōkṣamu Galadā
records.pallavi: Mōkṣamu galadā bhuvilō jīvanmuktulu gāni vāralaku
records.meaning: Asks whether liberation is possible at all for those who are not already free while living — and answers that music itself is the path.
records.notes: The charanam names bhakti, saṅgīta and jñāna together. Sāramati's four-note descent is what makes the piece sound like it is looking inward.

records.title: Nā Jīvādhāra
records.meaning: Calls Rama the very support of his life, then asks why he is being ignored.

records.title: Nagumōmu Galavāni
records.meaning: Longs for one glimpse of the smiling-faced Lord who has stolen his heart, and asks Garuda to carry the message.
records.notes: Probably the single most-performed Tyagaraja kriti. The anupallavi asks Garuda why he has not brought Rama — that address is the emotional hinge of the piece.

records.title: Nannu Pālimpa
records.meaning: Asks whether Rama has actually walked all this way just to look after him.
records.notes: Mōhanaṃ with no half-notes at all — one of the safest first concert pieces, and still substantial enough for swaram.

records.title: Nannu Viḍaci
records.meaning: Begs Rama not to move a step away and leave him behind.
records.notes: Rītigauḷa is all curves and no straight lines; this kriti is the usual vehicle for learning them. Miśra cāpu keeps the phrases from settling.

records.title: Nī Bhajana Gāna
records.pallavi: Nī bhajana gāna rasikula nīvē kāvavē
records.meaning: Asks Rama to protect those who take delight in singing his praise.

records.title: Nidhi Cāla Sukhamā
records.pallavi: Nidhi cāla sukhamā rāmuni sannidhi sēva sukhamā
records.pallavi_telugu: నిధి చాల సుఖమా రాముని సన్నిధి సేవ సుఖమా
records.meaning: Which is the real comfort — a hoard of wealth, or standing in Rama's presence? Written when Tyagaraja refused the Tanjore court's patronage.
records.notes: The biographical kriti: his answer to the king's invitation. Short, and the whole argument sits in the pallavi.

records.title: Ninnē Bhajana
records.meaning: A vow to worship no one but Rama.

records.title: Ō Raṅgaśāyī
records.meaning: Calls out to Ranganatha at Srirangam and asks why, when called, he does not answer.
records.notes: Composed at the Srirangam temple gate. A full-length Kāmbhōji main piece — the charanam's madhyama-kāla passage is the famous stretch.

records.title: Paramātmuḍu Veligē
records.meaning: Says the supreme self shines in everything — in every creature, in every element — and asks the listener to grasp it properly.
records.notes: The most explicitly advaitic of the well-known kritis. Vāgadhīśvari (34th mēḷa) is almost unused elsewhere.

records.title: Rāgasudhārasa
records.pallavi: Rāgasudhārasa pānamu jēsi rājillavē ō manasā
records.meaning: Urges the mind to drink the nectar of rāga and shine — devotion through music rather than ritual.
records.notes: One of the nāda-upāsana group where Tyagaraja argues that music is itself the sādhana. Āndōḷikā rocks gently, which suits the argument.

records.title: Rāma Bhakti Sāmrājya
records.meaning: Calls devotion to Rama an empire in itself — the only sovereignty worth holding.

records.title: Rāma Kathā Sudhā
records.meaning: Drinking the nectar of Rama's story is worth more, he says, than any other draught.
records.notes: Madhyamāvati is traditionally a closing rāga, so this often ends a concert.

records.title: Rāma Nannu Brōvarā
records.meaning: A plain, direct appeal: protect me, prince Rama.

records.title: Rāma Nī Samānam Evaru
records.pallavi: Rāma nī samānam evaru raghuvaṃśa sudhāmbudhi candra
records.pallavi_telugu: రామ నీ సమానమెవరు రఘువంశ సుధాంబుధి చంద్ర
records.meaning: Asks who could possibly equal Rama, moon of the nectar-ocean of the Raghu line.
records.notes: The standard Kharaharapriya main piece for students — long enough to carry niraval and swaram, plain enough that the rāga stays audible.

records.title: Sādhiñcanē
records.meaning: Tells the mind that Rama got his way — a half-affectionate complaint that the Lord always does exactly as he pleases.
records.notes: Famous for its tone: the composer scolds Rama through the charanams, ending with the line about Yasoda. Ārabhi's clean lines expose any slack in the tala.

records.title: Sāmaja Vara Gamana
records.pallavi: Sāmaja vara gamana sādhu hṛt sārasābja pālita
records.meaning: Praises the Lord whose gait is majestic as an elephant's, who tends the lotus-hearts of the good.
records.notes: Sanskrit sāhityam, Hindōḷaṃ's five notes, and a tune that sits comfortably — which is why it turns up in almost every student's first concert set.

records.title: Śāmbhō Mahādēva
records.meaning: Salutes Siva as the great god, consort of Girija.
records.notes: Pantuvarāḷi here is the modern name for the 51st mēḷa Kāmavardhini — not the 45th mēḷa Śubhapantuvarāḷi.

records.title: Sārasa Sāma Dāna
records.pallavi: Sārasa sāma dāna bhēda daṇḍa catura
records.meaning: Praises Rama as adept in all four instruments of statecraft — conciliation, gifts, division and force.
records.notes: One of the rare kritis whose imagery is political rather than devotional. Kāpī Nārāyaṇi should not be confused with Kāpi.

records.title: Sītamma Māyamma
records.pallavi: Sītamma māyamma śrī rāmuḍu mā taṇḍri
records.meaning: Sita is our mother and Rama our father — the household framing that makes this one of the most-loved of the festival kirtanas.
records.notes: Short, warm and almost always the first utsava sampradāya kīrtana a student learns.

records.title: Śōbhillu Saptasvara
records.meaning: Tells the mind to worship the seven beautiful swaras, which shine in the navel, heart, throat, tongue and nose.
records.notes: A kriti about music itself — it names where each svara resonates in the body. Common early-concert opener.

records.title: Sogasu Jūḍa Taramā
records.pallavi: Sogasu jūḍa taramā nī sogasu jūḍa taramā
records.meaning: Asks whether it is even possible to take in the Lord's beauty — the eye cannot hold it.
records.notes: Commonly listed in Kannaḍagauḷa; some editions place it in Kānaḍā, and the two are handled here under one reference entry. Worth confirming with your teacher.

records.title: Śrī Gaṇapatini Sēvimparārē
records.meaning: Urges the mind to worship Lord Ganapati, the remover of obstacles.

records.title: Śrī Nārada
records.meaning: Salutes Narada as the bee at the lotus of nāda — the sage who gave Tyagaraja his music.
records.notes: Tyagaraja composed several kritis on Narada after receiving the Svārārṇava text; this is the best known. Kānaḍā is learnt by imitation, not from its scale.

records.title: Śrī Raghuvara Sugunālaya
records.meaning: Addresses Rama as the dwelling-place of every good quality.
records.notes: A weighty Bhairavi piece; good practice ground for the rāga's D2-in-ascent, D1-in-descent asymmetry.

records.title: Śrī Rāma Jaya Rāma
records.pallavi: Śrī rāma jaya rāma śṛṅgāra rāma
records.meaning: A name-chant on Rama in his beauty — built for a group to sing together, not for solo display.
records.notes: Typical divya nāma construction: a short repeating tune, the work carried by the names rather than by melodic variation.

records.title: Śrī Subrahmaṇyāya Namastē
records.meaning: Salutations to Subrahmanya — one of Tyagaraja's handful of Sanskrit kritis on a deity other than Rama.
records.notes: A substantial Kāmbhōji piece; often taken as the main item, with the anupallavi's madhyama-kāla passage as the highlight.

records.title: Sujana Jīvana
records.meaning: Rama is the very life of good people.
records.notes: Khamās sits low and warm; this is a common second-item choice.

records.title: Teliyalēru Rāma
records.meaning: Says that people cannot recognise the path of devotion, however much they argue about it.
records.notes: Dhēnuka (9th mēḷa) is otherwise barely used; this kriti is effectively the rāga's calling card.

records.title: Tera Tīyagarādā
records.meaning: Asks Venkataramana of Tirupati to draw aside the curtain — outwardly the temple screen, inwardly the veil of ego.
records.notes: The double meaning of "tera" — temple curtain and the veil of the ego — is the whole kriti. Commonly listed in Gauḷipantu; some editions give Gauḷa, and the reference entry here is Gauḷa.

records.title: Uṇḍēdi Rāmuḍokaḍu
records.meaning: There is only one Rama — a flat statement of exclusive devotion.

records.title: Vandanamu Raghunandana
records.meaning: Salutations to the delight of the Raghus, who bridged the sea.
records.notes: Sahānā's gamakas are the point here — sung plainly the kriti loses its character entirely.

records.title: Vara Līla Gāna Lōla
records.pallavi: Vara līla gāna lōla sura pāla suguṇa jāla
records.meaning: Praises the Lord absorbed in the song of his own play — a Sanskrit kriti dense with internal rhyme.

records.title: Yōcanā Kamala Lōcanā
records.meaning: Asks the lotus-eyed one what thought is holding him back from granting his devotee.
